plans.note: Section 7 is headed 'Limitations of Liability'; check whether the cap is mutual, whether an amount is stated, and whether carve-outs (IP infringement, confidentiality, indemnity, willful misconduct) survive. Coordinate with INDEMN so the same term is not flagged twice.

Heading points to 'Indemnification of Contractor' only — i.e., a one-way indemnity running against us. Confirm no vendor-side IP/misconduct indemnity appears elsewhere (sec-4 ownership, sec-5 warranties) before treating the vendor indemnity as missing and the customer indemnity as over-broad.
No restrictive-covenants section in the outline; scan the purpose/engagement scope in sec-1 and termination survival in sec-6 for any embedded restriction on our business or sourcing.
Check sec-1 purpose language for sole/exclusive provider wording and sec-3 compensation for fees triggered by using other suppliers; otherwise absent and no action needed.
Pricing sits in sec-3; look for any obligation on us to extend best terms to the Contractor. MFN in our favour would be beneficial and is not flagged.

No standalone personnel clause listed; consultant agreements often place a no-hire in the engagement or termination sections, so check sec-1 and sec-6 for duration and a general-advertising carve-out.

Section 6 governs termination: confirm we may terminate for convenience on reasonable notice without penalty, and that the Contractor cannot terminate at will mid-engagement. Check treatment of fees for work performed to date.
No term/renewal heading appears; term and any auto-renewal, notice window and uplift may be embedded in sec-6 or in the sec-1 engagement description.
No miscellaneous/general provisions section is in the outline; check the preamble recitals and the tail of sec-7 for choice of law, venue or arbitration before recording as missing.
No assignment heading; look for assignment/change-of-control language in sec-6 termination triggers and in the preamble party block.

Section 4 covers ownership of materials and acceptance — confirm deliverables vest in us (work made for hire plus present assignment), that our data and pre-existing IP stay ours, and that ownership is not conditioned on full payment beyond the fallback.
Any licence-back of Contractor background or third-party materials will sit in sec-4; test scope for affiliates and contractors, irrevocability and perpetuity.
No audit heading; check sec-3 for records/inspection tied to fees and sec-4 for verification of use. Vendor audits of us must be notified, infrequent and at Vendor cost.
Watch sec-3 for late-payment penalties or kill fees and sec-6 for early-termination charges payable by us; service credits running to us are welcome and not flagged.

Section 5 pairs representations with a warranty disclaimer — assess whether the Services warranty (conformity to Specifications) has a meaningful duration and re-performance/refund remedy, and whether the disclaimer swallows it.

No insurance heading; check sec-5 representations and sec-7 risk allocation for any coverage undertaking. If the Contractor handles our data or attends our premises, standard coverages should be added.
Review sec-3 compensation for minimum hours, retainers or take-or-pay commitments and sec-1 for committed volumes; an exit right is required if any commitment exists.
Section 6 is the natural home for wind-down duties and sec-4 for delivery of materials on termination; if neither provides data return and transition assistance, record as missing.
